item.description: Two Chelsea stars could return in time for Liverpool cup clash Chelsea Injury News Ahead of Liverpool Carabao Cup Clash Chelsea go to Anfield with a problem that is simple enough to understand. They have injuries in key areas, they have a suspension to deal with and they are coming off a poor 2-0 defeat to Tottenham at Stamford Bridge. Momentum can disappear quickly in football, and that is exactly what has happened here. Back-to-back wins after the international break had improved the mood. Then came the loss to Spurs, and with it a fresh wave of concern around availability. Xabi Alonso now has to prepare for a Carabao Cup tie against Liverpool, followed almost immediately by a league game against Manchester United. Squad management matters, but so does simply having enough reliable bodies fit and available. The biggest issue is not one injury, it is the number of them. Chelsea are missing senior players, they are waiting on scan results in one case, and they have another first-team regular serving a suspension. Morgan Rogers led the line, with Geovany Quenda brought into the front line, while other attacking alternatives stayed out of the starting picture. That told its own story. item.title: Mbappé loses brand deals in China over alleged Mao meme remarks
item.description: French soccer player Kylian Mbappe’s image appears on the label of a sports drink produced by a Chinese manufacturer. (is associated with: «Mbappé loses brand deals in China over alleged Mao meme remarks») Johannes Neudecker/dpa Two beverage companies in China are ending their partnerships with French football star Kylian Mbappé effective immediately. In their respective statements, both companies said they would not tolerate behaviour that offends the feelings of the Chinese people. However, the companies did not provide any further details on how Mbappé allegedly behaved inappropriately. Chinese media outlets also didn't explain the companies' decision and merely referred to statements made by Mbappé in interviews. Remarks allegedly made by the French player during a podcast interview have been circulating online. In a video that emerged on Monday, Mbappé was asked about his favourite meme featuring himself. He then mentioned one where his face had been photoshopped on to that of "some guy - I think he's a Chinese dictator." There are, for a fact, memes featuring Mbappé's face superimposed on an image of Chinese revolutionary leader Mao Zedong. As one of the founders of the People's Republic, Mao is held in high esteem in China. Content critical of China's political leaders is generally heavily censored in the country. The Real Madrid forward had advertising deals with a sports drink manufacturer based in Shenzhen, southern China, and a company from Inner Mongolia that is well known in China for its dairy products. Among other things, his face appeared on the bottle labels. A second dairy product manufacturer and the influential social media platform Xiaohongshu - the equivalent of Instagram in China - also announced they were ending their partnerships with Mbappé. Meanwhile, China’s state-run television stopped airing commercials featuring the player. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun emphasized that words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people would, of course, be met with united opposition from all sectors of Chinese society. The Spanish La Liga, meanwhile, said it "deeply regrets the offence caused" by the comments and stressed that they "were made in a personal capacity and do not represent" the league. "Spanish football upholds respect, coexistence, and unity among people of all cultures. We convey our respect to China, its institutions, and its people, and we deeply value the support of the millions of fans who follow us each week," it said in a statement.

item.title: James Dolan urged to ‘shut up’ after New York Knicks’ 0-3 start to championship defense
item.description: Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images New York Knicks team owner James Dolan’s influence over his championship-winning team has come under question after a 0-3 start to the 2026-27 NBA season. The Knicks stunned the world by storming to the 2026 NBA Championship behind an incredible playoff run. However, they have not looked like a championship-winning organisation since then. After getting squeezed in free agency because team owner Dolan publicly outlined that the team will not go into the second apron of the NBA salary cap, which has since hurt negotiations with extension-eligible players, and cannonballed into a terrible start to the season. ESPN analyst tells James Dolan to ‘shut up’ after causing Knicks drama ESPN’s Tim MacMahon openly called out Dolan after the team’s 111-102 loss to the Orlando Magic, dropping them to 0-3 to start the season. “They need James Dolan to shut up. That’s what they need. There’s too much drama; There are too many distractions. Leave it to James Dolan to suck the joy out of a post-championship thing.” “Going back to before the parade: ‘Oh, the second apron is a concrete wall.’ The preseason declaration that none of the guys up for extension are getting paid. The phishing email… The ring night. The biggest thing the Knicks have to overcome is bad ownership.” The salary cap statement already led to the longest-tenured Knicks player, Mitchell Robinson, leaving for divisional rivals in the Boston Celtics. Karl-Anthony Towns, Miles McBride and Josh Hart await contract extensions after a title-winning year but have been told that no in-season negotiations will take place, souring the mood of key players as they hope to become the first team to defend an NBA Championship in eight years. The Knicks have lost to the Philadelphia 76ers, Celtics, and Magic, but will hope to end their losing streak against the 3-0 Detroit Pistons on October 27. Dolan’s years of stepping away from the spotlight as the chief decision-maker for the Knicks led to a title-winning team being created for him. Now, he has to toe the line between celebrating his greatest achievement as a team owner and keeping the strong harmony that led to the title win in the first place. item.title: Kylian Mbappé ‘sincerely sorry’ for ‘ill-judged’ Mao Zedong comment
item.description: Kylian Mbappé ‘sincerely sorry’ for ‘ill-judged’ Mao Zedong comment Kylian Mbappé (27) has apologised for a comment in which he referred to former China Chairman Mao Zedong as a “dictator”. It follows swift backlash from Chinese sponsors. Mbappé’s comments about Mao came during an appearance on the show The Bridge. Mbappé said that the funniest meme he had seen of him was the one where his face is photoshopped onto that of Mao Zedong. “ I think he’s a Chinese dictator ,” he said, before revealing that he would send the image to friends. Mao Zedong was not specifically named in the video, which was taken down. Energy drink company Dongpeng and dairy producer Meigniu both announced the termination of their sponsorship deals with Mbappé, stating that his “ behaviour offends national sentiment “. It was also announced that games in which Mbappé participates would not be broadcast in China. Real Madrid’s games in La Liga would naturally be affected. The league put out a statement on Tuesday morning stating that they “deeply regret the offence caused by Kylian Mbappé’s recent comments among Chinese fans. Those comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga,” read an official statement. “We apologise on behalf of La Liga and all its clubs.” Mbappé has now also made his apology, shared on X in English, Mandarin, and French. “During a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself. My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset. That was absolutely not my intention. “I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry,” added the France captain. The controversy comes in the wake of Monday night’s Ballon d’Or ceremony. The Real Madrid forward was one of the favourites to win the trophy, which was awarded to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane. item.description: France and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe arrives at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London (FRANCK FIFE) Kylian Mbappe apologised on Tuesday after the Real Madrid star was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain's La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of "some guy -- I think he's a Chinese dictator". This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. "My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset," French forward Mbappe said in a statement in French, Chinese and English. Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga." In China, jokes about Mao, the country's founding leader who died in 1976 -- and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths -- remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year's World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sport drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments," Dongpeng said in a statement. Mengniu, China's largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of social media followers. "Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe" was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said the "extremely serious wrong remarks... crossed the red line" and others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe's image from their bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China's biggest online football outlets, said Mbappe's remarks were "offensive to China and the Chinese people". - Furore - In an interview with French sports newspaper L'Equipe, the 27-year-old Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator. "There's a part of it that's funny... but there is another part that's a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history," he said. item.description: A backlash has erupted on Chinese social media over Mbappé's comments on a "Chinese dictator" [Getty Images] Kylian Mbappé has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands. Mbappé had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the programme cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao. The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football. The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead. A few people came out in support of him on Chinese social media, but that is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics. Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like Mbappé. item.title: Shannon Sharpe offers brutal two-word response to Dak Prescott vs. John Elway comparison
item.description: Credit: Dustin Bradford/Cooper Neill via Getty Images After a fan in Shannon Sharpe’s replies compared the Cowboys QB to his former superstar teammate, the Hall Of Famer gave a blunt reply. John Elway is an NFL legend in every sense of the word. A two-time Super Bowl champion, Super Bowl XXXIII MVP and 1987 NFL MVP, Elway was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2004. He is considered by many to be the greatest player in Denver Broncos history. While Elway himself isn’t in the limelight these past few years, his former teammate Shannon Sharpe is. And when one fan in particular replied to one of Sharpe’s posts with a claim about Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, the tight end quickly put him in his place. Shannon Sharpe suggests Dak Prescott isn’t better than John Elway at anything Prescott is yet to even start comparing to Elway’s postseason résumé, with a 2-5 playoff record and no Super Bowl appearances. Elway went 14-8 in the playoffs, reached five Super Bowls and won two. While Dak has been great in the regular season, he doesn’t have an MVP or a Super Bowl MVP. So when a fan in response to one of Sharpe’s posts suggested that Prescott is better than Elway, the former Broncos man had a simple but effective response. “At what?” was all Sharpe asked in reply to the fan’s post which read, “Dak better than Elway.” The numbers and the accolades speak for themselves, and Prescott will need a lot more hardware if he is to be counted among the greatest quarterbacks of all time. The Cowboys are 3-4 after Week 7 of the 2026-27 NFL season, and they need to put together a run of wins if they are going to make themselves look like contenders again. If Dak is finally able to deliver some postseason success, then these conversations can perhaps be entertained a bit more. item.title: 🍔 TikToks & comfort eating?! Yamal's reaction to his Ballon d'Or defeat
item.description: 🍔 TikToks & comfort eating?! Yamal's reaction to his Ballon d'Or defeat Quite a few observers gave Spain's young star Lamine Yamal a serious chance of winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or. Since last night, though, one thing is clear: he has not (yet) done enough to claim football's most prestigious prize, with both winner Harry Kane and runner-up Kylian Mbappé finishing ahead of him. While the 19-year-old still looked a little dejected at the ceremony itself after being named “only” the world's best young player for the third year running, his mood seemed to improve as the evening went on. Videos and photos on ‘X’ and ‘TikTok’ showed just that. His little brother did not seem particularly impressed with the event either. But as the night wore on, his mood seemed to improve. After the ceremony, he posted a video on ‘TikTok’ with his girlfriend, Inés García Santos. Perhaps an upcoming visit to a fast-food giant also had something to do with his improved mood. France Football chief Vincent Garcia offered a theory yesterday as to why Yamal finished only third. Speaking to the newspaper ‘L’Équipe’, he said the votes for the Spanish nominees had been “somewhat split”. Last year's winner Rodri finished fourth. The Spaniards' strong showing may therefore have cost Yamal crucial votes. “I think Rodri took votes away from Lamine in this year's voting,” Garcia said. Kylian Mbappé, incidentally, also seemed to take his defeat to Harry Kane pretty well in the end. As he left the event via the red carpet, a camera caught him playing a round of rock-paper-scissors. The Golden State Warriors haven’t done a great job of building a talented roster around Steph Curry this summer, and it has upset many fans. Curry is nearing the end of his career, and many believe he deserves a competitive team built around him. Golden State has arguably been the best team in the NBA over the last decade. Still, ESPN analyst Kendrick Perkins has urged Curry to move on from the Warriors. “Steph needs to be planning his exit strategy from the Golden State Warriors," said Perkins on 'NBA Today'. "Think about it, over the last four years, the Warriors have been in the play-in tournament. And this year, the way that the West is stacked up, they're gonna be a play-in tournament team again. You can't waste any more time hoping and banking that Mike Dunleavy is gonna get it right or is gonna make the moves that are needed to make sure that you can compete for a title, especially in a tough Western Conference." Warriors head coach Steve Kerr also had plenty to say about the organization’s approach to building around Curry. “Do we throw away our entire future to build around a 39-year-old Steph? He turns 39 in March, right? Does it make sense now to throw away all those picks? H*ll no," Kerr said. That reflects the situation Golden State faces with its current roster. Former Warriors big man DeMarcus Cousins recently went after general manager Mike Dunleavy, criticizing his efforts to build a competitive team around Curry. “I think [Mike] Dunleavy has done a sh*t job as far as putting a roster around Steph Curry. Why this guy still has a job, I'll never know. They're still running the same outdated system as far as going extremely small... it doesn't work anymore. The system is outdated,” Cousins said. The last couple of seasons have been disappointing for the Warriors, to say the least. However, expectations remain high because fans grew accustomed to a decade of success. Now, former players are calling out the organization for failing to make the moves needed to give its franchise superstar another legitimate championship run. Curry is nearing the end of his career, but Golden State appears increasingly focused on its future. Cousins and several others are frustrated with what they see as the Warriors conceding the remainder of Curry’s NBA career rather than doing more to compete while he is still playing at a high level. The Los Angeles Lakers underwent significant roster changes this summer as they embraced a new approach to building around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. The duo is now officially the face of the franchise. That shift meant parting ways with several players Lakers fans had grown accustomed to seeing over the years. One of the biggest names was Rui Hachimura, who signed with the cross-town rival Los Angeles Clippers. “Free agent Rui Hachimura has agreed to a two-year, $28 million deal to sign with the LA Clippers , sources tell ESPN. Hachimura and his agent Darren Matsubara of THE•TEAM came to an understanding with the Clippers early in free agency on finding a deal together. The sides waited for the Lakers to complete their offseason business to pursue a sign-and-trade, but the Lakers didn't cooperate on one, according to a source close to Hachimura," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote. During the summer, Hachimura discussed why he chose to sign with the Clippers. "Above all, being able to stay in LA is the best outcome for me," Hachimura said. "They support their players of course, their families and inner circles from what I hear. Plus they have a brand new arena with advanced physical and medical support and all kinds of useful tools for physical training. I'm really looking forward to all of it." On Monday, the former Lakers Swiss Army knife revealed the harsh reality of playing in Los Angeles and explained why the pressure can be so difficult to handle. “They think that [only] one season, I was good, but I keep doing it. I consistently — like three years in a row — was shooting 45 percent on threes and 50 or 60 percent from mid-range, and I was always top five in shooting for three years. It's, of course, because of the team and how we operated. We had LeBron [James], [Anthony Davis], Luka [Doncic],” Hachimura told ClutchPoints. “But also, it's tough to play for the Lakers. It's a big crowd, big shine. The lights are brighter. The thing I always say is that I've always had that, but it's just what the team's situation is.” There is no doubt that satisfying the Lakers faithful is difficult, as they are one of the most passionate fan bases in all of sports. The franchise faces enormous expectations to field a competitive team and make a deep playoff run every season. item.title: Carrick to stay in charge of Man Utd for Chelsea game
item.description: Michael Carrick signed a two-year deal with the club last May [Press Association] Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their trip to Chelsea this weekend. Sources have told BBC Sport that the 45-year-old will be given the opportunity to turn things around at Old Trafford following a dismal start to the campaign. Carrick oversaw training on Tuesday morning, as United look to end a run of eight matches without a win in all competitions when they visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Sunday's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford plunged Carrick's future into doubt, with United sitting one place above the relegation zone. It is understood United's hierarchy have explored the possibility of replacing Carrick, with ex-Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann under consideration. But sources have told BBC Sport that the former Middlesbrough manager will not only take charge against Chelsea but will also be given a chance to revive the club's fortunes on the pitch. Carrick took interim charge in January following Ruben Amorim's departure and he was rewarded with the permanent job in May after securing Champions League qualification with an impressive run that resulted in them finishing third. But United's form has collapsed this term, with Carrick's side winning just one of their eight Premier League matches so far this season. Defender Lisandro Martinez criticised the club's board for a lack of investment following United's 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League earlier this month. Captain Bruno Fernandes then took aim at Carrick's tactics following a humiliating 4-1 loss against Como in their next Champions League fixture. The Portuguese was dropped to the bench for Sunday's loss to Bournemouth, and remained an unused substitute. United supporters chanted Carrick's name as the former England international made his way to the tunnel after the match, but quickly directed boos at the players once Carrick had made his way off the pitch. Carrick gestured towards the Stretford End as they chanted his name after the match. "It wasn't a farewell from me," Carrick said on Sky Sports. "I've mixed emotions, I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment. "Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way. To have that connection with the supporters it's mixed emotions, it'll take a bit of time to digest but I certainly appreciate their support. "The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough." Carrick was at United's training ground on Monday morning, despite the first team being given the day off. Director of Football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada were both pictured arriving at the club's training ground, with Carrick leaving at around 5pm. Questions over Carrick remain - analysis Manche

item.description: How long is too long to hang on to a top fantasy draft pick who’s been decidedly underwhelming. When does name value merely represent sunk costs? And, most importantly, how do you chase away the regret that comes with watching one of your guys thrive on someone else’s roster as you sink to the bottom of the league? We can’t really help with that last one, but we can try and shed some light on the first two questions. In this week’s hold, drop, trade we’ll break down some players you might have invested a high value draft pick or pricey waiver wire bid in, only to be let down by inconsistent performances and single-digit scores. And, this week, that means taking a closer look at a certain Kansas City Chiefs quarterback. He’s turned nine catches the last two weeks into 40 yards. Is there someone in your league who is a sucker for lowkey name value or the Bengals’ offense? It wasn’t so much that life became easy at that level, but the direction was fairly obvious. Keep playing Challengers, improve the ranking, qualify for Grand Slams and eventually establish yourself on the ATP Tour. Going to university was something you considered before all that. Apparently, not anymore. On October 20, the University of Texas announced the signing of Rodrigo Pacheco Mendez, a 21-year-old Mexican who reached a career-high ranking of No. 196 last year and has spent several seasons competing professionally. He will join the Longhorns in January 2027. However, Dodig announced in October he would continue playing professional tennis and was not enrolling at Texas. And these are hardly isolated examples. item.title: Paul Finebaum takes shot at Brian Kelly’s ‘off-brand’ media roles
item.description: Photo Credit: ESPN College Football on YouTube Brian Kelly isn’t coaching college football this year for the first time since 1983. In his first season since he was fired as LSU’s head coach, he’s serving as an analyst for CBS Sports and College Sports Radio on SiriusXM . Kelly was one of many media members to weigh in on the Texas Longhorns and quarterback Arch Manning after consecutive losses to the Oklahoma Sooners and Florida Gators, putting the onus of the blame for Manning’s struggles on Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s playcalling. However, Manning and Sarkisian got things back on track on Saturday against the Ole Miss Rebels, winning 34-27, and on Monday, ESPN’s Paul Finebaum rebuked Kelly’s analysis. “It was on this day a year ago that Brian Kelly was fired,” Franklin said on The Matt Barrie Show . “(James) Franklin had already been fired. By the way, I want to congratulate Brian Kelly for calling out Steve Sarkisian this week. He picked a good week to show what a big-time Sirius XM radio analyst he is. Brian Kelly cannot do anything right, other than now I’m sure he’s trying to find one of these off-brand jobs to land.” ﻿ This season, Kelly co-hosts a weekly college football show for SiriusXM and calls games for CBS Sports on TV . Finebaum might not be far off the mark on Kelly’s attempting to land a coaching job. Kelly has said publicly that he still has a lot to give to college football and wants “to get back to building relationships and successful programs. ” Kelly has already had to address rumors that his name is being floated as a potential fit for the Rutgers Scarlet Knights amid head coach Greg Schiano’s poor start to the season. “You hate hearing the rumors, because that means somebody’s job is being evaluated,” he said earlier this season. “It’s uncomfortable for me. I don’t feel easy about it. I think we all know it’s something that gets out in the media and it’s talked about because it’s juicy, right? But, for me, I just focus on what I’m doing on a day-to-day basis. I don’t relish my name being mentioned for other jobs. I’m pulling for the guy that’s got that job, and I want to see him do well.” Ironically , Finebaum was also highly critical of Sarkisian’s “absolute arrogance” and the job he did with Manning himself after Texas’ Florida loss. “I’m beginning to wonder if Arch Manning should even start. I know he will, and he’s capable of leading them to a win, but I blame Sarkisian for every aspect of this,” Finebaum said before Texas’s win on Saturday. Texas has silenced its critics for now, but if things start to go poorly again for the Longhorns down the stretch, Kelly, Finebaum and everyone else in the peanut gallery will be right back to firing off their takes and assigning blame.
